summary: Confirmed both estimate records against PDF pp. 3-4 after reading the entire markdown conversion, extracting all eight PDF pages, and inspecting Figures 1-3 in memory. The document has no appendix. The frequentist GPT-minus-HUM coefficient (-0.11), SE (0.13), 95% confidence interval [-0.37, +0.16], p-value (.42), and accompanying TOST bound (0.33) match Section 4.1. The Bayesian posterior median (+0.06), 95% credible interval [-0.06, +0.20], Bayes factor BF_01 (10.95), and Normal(0, 1) prior also match Section 4.1. These are alternative analyses of the same paired comparison, as the extraction explicitly records. The Bayesian interval is identified as a credible interval and is not treated as a frequentist standard error. The printed cohort count of 62 supports the study and within-person arm randomized counts; analysis-specific participant and rating counts are not printed, so the estimate counts appropriately remain null. Question, construct, measure, unit, direction, AI availability, timing, within-person design, comparison type, and participant basis of uncertainty agree with the randomized session order, originality rating protocol, and subject random-intercept model. No eligible full-sample outcome or contrast is missing under extraction rules 4-6: Figure 3 and the top-quality/failure results are subgroup or moderation analyses; seed-set assignment is not stated to be randomized; trait and perception results are associations; utility and solo-AUT contrasts are not reported. The later seed analysis is restricted to CON-first participants and combines subsequent HUM and GPT outcomes. The extraction correctly documents the paper’s inconsistent corpus/rater counts and unexplained difference between its frequentist and Bayesian estimates without replacing or recomputing them.
